text: {"score":4,"justification":"The summary is accurate and well grounded, with specific numbers (35.0% vs 6.3% expected, z 5.45, 6% low-complexity 99215s, 4 of 4 documented 99215s supported). It uses cautious, inconclusive language and flags thin documentation. The claims cited fit their sentences: C0104160 had high MDM, C0103880/C0103939 are Z09-only, and C0103348 is R10.9-only. Weaknesses: the formal next_steps are generic and omit the specific, more actionable steps in the rationale (request charts for the low-complexity 99215s). The summary also has a few small inaccuracies and inconsistencies.","problems":["next_steps are generic (larger sample, re-screen) and do not name the low-complexity 99215 claims or the Z09-only visits, which the rationale does recommend; the two parts are inconsistent.","The headline says 99215 is above expectation 'in every complexity tier', but the card only gives the provider's share vs the all-provider share per tier, so the wording is somewhat loose; it is supported by the table though.","'14% for comparison providers' is correct for 99215 (0.143), but the 14% is derived from the all-provider rate, which may include this provider.","The recommendation to sample mid-complexity (2 to 3 conditions) patients is only weakly tied to the evidence; the excess is larger in higher tiers by ratio.","Examples listed include C0103599, a 99214 below-billed claim, which does not support the 99215 narrative; C0103322 (AF, 1 condition) is a weaker low-complexity example than the Z09-only claims discussed in the text.","Does not note that C0104160 appears in both the high-complexity list and the documented-supported list in a way that makes it the only overlap; the 3 other supported 99215 charts are not in the sampled claims."]}
